(the repo file is never mutated). CHANGELOG.md in-repo is curated-only:
  PRs add lines under `## Unreleased`; `scripts/release_notes.sh` picks
  curated `## <version>` → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional
  commits since the previous tag. The pub.dev 262144-byte changelog cap is
  enforced on the STAGED file (oldest staged sections trim), so it can
  never block a release again — the publish job's repo-file check is
  ADVISORY (`::warning::` pointing at `CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md`), never a
  hard gate (gh-1522 rework, PR #1526).
- **App builds** — `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive
  `latest tag + 1` and pass it via `--build-name`/`--build-number`
  (BUILD_NUMBER = run number); the fastlane `store_pubspec_version` helper
  prefers the derived `BUILD_NAME` env.
- **Local / CLI** — `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe --tags`; `fa --version` reads the stamped `version.txt`
  first, the placeholder pubspec second (a plain `dart run` shows
  `0.0.0-dev` — self-explanatory).

Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs are input-gated: `releaseDryRun: true`
exercises the whole pipeline without the tag push (AC1), and
`releaseDispatch: true` on `refs/heads/main` is the real release — bare
validation dispatches (the SM's per-PR `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref
<branch>`) arm nothing. Since gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI run,
ci.yml has no main-push trigger at all: merging to main fires NO CI and
cuts NO tag — the release job arms on the 2h coalesce schedule (≤1 release
per 2h, catching up merged commits) and on `releaseDispatch` only. The
release checklist is: wait for a schedule tick (or fire `releaseDispatch`)
→ watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag → watch
the tag-scoped `publish`/`binaries` jobs. The daily:

- lets `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive their version
  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- **never lets a leg REST-mint a missing release tag** (gh-2026): a
  `gh release create vX --draft` on a tag that does not exist yet mints a
  lightweight API tag with NO push event, so the ci.yml tag train never
  fires and the draft is stranded (the v0.1.408 silent class, issue #597 —
  recurred as v1.0.663 / v1.0.665, whose minted pushes also rode
  actions/checkout's persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader). Both
  `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` and `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`
  probe `git ls-remote --exit-code` first and, when the ref is definitely
  missing, mint through `scripts/release_tag_mint.sh`: an annotated tag
  pushed via token-URL with the PAT the job already carries
  (`GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT` on the dispatch-time call sites), the persisted
  extraheader stripped, and the train start verified with
  `gh run list --branch <tag>` BEFORE any draft is created — a mint whose
  train does not start fails the leg loudly instead of stranding a draft
  for the sweeper. The probe authenticates with the RELEASE_PAT (`gh`
  prefers `GH_TOKEN`), so the PAT itself needs `actions: read`; the job
  tokens carry the grant too (uniformly on every mint-reachable job) as
  defense-in-depth in case the probe is ever switched to the job token,
  and a failing probe is reported as its own error — never read as "no
  train". The mint tolerates the raced-mint push (a sibling leg landing
  the same tag first — the 2-arch `build-macos-cli` matrix plus
  `build-extension` race the same fresh tag) by re-probing the ref, and
  rolls an untrained tag back before failing so the prescribed re-run
  re-mints instead of stranding the draft. Identity note (vs the AGENTS.md

# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs dart format >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  printf '%s\n' "$STAGED_DART" | xargs git add --
  UNFORMATTED=$(dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed $STAGED_DART 2>/dev/null | grep '^Changed' || true)
  if [ -n "$UNFORMATTED" ]; then
    echo "❌ dart format could not fix these files (syntax error?):"
    echo "$UNFORMATTED"
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# THE shared fast gate (same script, same path filters as CI). --hook makes
# it derive the scope from the STAGED diff. It unsets GIT_* env itself

bash scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --hook

# no dispatch, and the release train sat red on the missing
    # fa-macos-arm64.tar.gz (gh-1832 refused to sign, pin_release refused
    # to move vpinned) until a manual rerun. With the producers in
    # `needs`, the same kill shape (cancelled job + cancelled checkout
    # step + no failed step — verified against the real run's jobs JSON)
    # trips the scan and the gh-2290 tag-arm dispatch rebuilds the
    # missing asset on a fresh allocation. Skipped producers (PR arm,
    # deduped twins) satisfy `needs` as `skipped` — no added latency
    # there.
    needs: [changes, static, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, test-faui, app-crap-gate, pty-integration-linux, pty-visual, binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    # Same-repo PRs: the empty-commit retrigger pushes to the PR branch,
    # which this token cannot do for a fork's ref. Tag pushes: the
    # release gate (gh-2290).
    if: always() && ((github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) || (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')))
    permissions:
      actions: write # gh workflow run — the tag-arm retrigger (gh-2290)
      contents: write
    steps:
      # gh-2290: the trip decision runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's
      # empty workspace has no scripts/ (the exit-127 class reddened the
      # dedupe pre-check on every arm, runs 38696670029/38696668627). The
      # checkout must be UNCONDITIONAL — the trip step runs on every arm
      # this job reaches, and a skipped checkout would empty the trip
      # output. Shallow: the script never reads history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      # One jobs call in a SINGLE valid document (steps arrays are
      # embedded per job — no per-job follow-ups; `gh api --paginate`
      # concatenates page bodies and jq then reads only the first page —
      # verified against a 69-job run), then the extracted,
      # fixture-self-tested trip decision (scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh;
      # static-gate selftest: scripts/watchdog_trip_selftest.sh). It trips
      # ONLY on the degraded-runner-kill signature — job conclusion
      # `failure` OR `cancelled` (the v1.0.745 kill landed as plain
      # `cancelled`) with at least one `cancelled` step or one UNCONCLUDED
      # (`null`) step (gh-2358: the v1.0.759 runner death froze the
      # mid-flight `flutter build ios` step — and every trailing step — at
      # `null`, invisible to a `cancelled`-step-only detector) and NO
      # `failed` step (a real test failure ends with a failed step,
      # including death after a real red — only the trailing steps freeze)
      # — and never on a real test failure, a skip, or a cancelled
      # never-started job.
      - name: Detect a timeout-type failure
        id: trip
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh run view "$RUN_ID" --repo "$REPO" --json jobs > watchdog-jobs.json
          bash scripts/watchdog_trip_check.sh watchdog-jobs.json

      # ── PR arm: empty-commit push (unchanged remedy) ──────────────────
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger workflows — the retrigger must
          # re-fire CI, so it rides RELEASE_PAT (same as release/gardener).
          token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}

      - name: Retrigger with an empty commit (fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          HAS_PAT: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT != '' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$HAS_PAT" != "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::RELEASE_PAT not configured — cannot retrigger"
            exit 0
          fi
          msg="ci: watchdog retrigger (degraded runner pool)"
          if [ "$(git log -1 --format=%s)" = "$msg" ]; then
            echo "head commit is already a watchdog retrigger — not looping"
            exit 0
          fi
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit --allow-empty -m "$msg"
          git push origin HEAD:"${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"

      # ── Tag arm (gh-2290): dispatch a fresh gate run on the tag ref ────
      # ONE retrigger max per tag (issue #194 loop-guard rule): a prior
      # workflow_dispatch run for this tag ref means the retrigger already
      # fired for this kill — never chain dispatches on a stuck pool.
      - name: Retrigger the tag gate (dispatch, fresh runner allocation)
        if: steps.trip.outputs.trip == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          prior=$(gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$REF" \
            --event workflow_dispatch \
            --json databaseId --jq 'length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
          if [ "${prior:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::a workflow_dispatch gate run already exists for $REF — not re-firing (one retrigger max per tag, gh-2290)"
            exit 0
          fi
          gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"
          echo "::notice::dispatched a fresh ci.yml gate run on $REF (watchdog degraded-runner retrigger, gh-2290)"

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2462

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: PR #2438 reached main with zero ci.yml runs on its final tree and a real
god-file violation (`flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings.dart` at 2801 > 2800
lines), because a cancelled ci.yml run was misread as a validation failure and
the SM then deadlocked itself out of re-validating.

**Root cause**:

- **Defect A (park logic input)** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: both aggregate
  jobs that carry required-check conclusions arm on `if: always()` without a
  cancellation guard:
  - `quality-gate` (line ~3957): `if: always() && needs.release-pending...`
  - `binaries-smoke-gate` (line ~5635): `if: always() && (pull_request || workflow_dispatch)`
  When the run was cancelled (run 46050811851, 2026-11-27 18:37Z), GitHub's
  `if: always()` started these jobs against legs concluded `cancelled`; the
  gate step's `fail()` classifies every non-`success`/non-`skipped` leg as a
  blocker, so the aggregate check-run concluded **failure** — a cancelled run,
  which is a *non-verdict*, was delivered to the SM as a *failure verdict*.
  SM tick 46054697279 then parked #2438 with `validation_failed` (19:10:20Z).
  The park-clearing rule lives in the external factory
  (`dmtools-agentic-workflows/factory-sm.yml`, tracked `@main` — not in this
  repo): it accepts only a HUMAN push newer than the park, while the same
  tick's silent-update push (merge commit `2a8eb3c9`, 19:10:46Z) rode a token
  that triggers no workflows and, even when re-kicking the SM, could not clear
  its own park — the self-deadlock. Human merge of `fb6543e0796e` (19:12:57Z)
  hit a tree no successful dispatch covered; `sm-merge-guard.yml` filed #2457
  (the guard was RIGHT).
- **Defect B (loc ceiling)** — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/settings.dart`
  grew 2792 → 2801 in `fb6543e0796e`. The loc ceiling (2800, wc -l semantics)
  is enforced by `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml` `gates.loc` in CI's
  `app-crap-gate` job — which never ran, because Defect A cancelled the only
  validation dispatch on that final tree. The enforcement belt had no
  repo-side (test-suite-level) check that runs on every ci.yml dispatch
  regardless of path: `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` scopes the loc/crap stages to
  lib/bin (core) only, so flutter_app files depended solely on the one CI job
  the SM deadlock skipped.

**Impact**: any cancelled ci.yml run (concurrency cancel, manual cancel, pool
kill) parks its PR with a false `validation_failed`; combined with the SM's
own silent-update push this produces an unvalidated-merge trap that a human
merge turns into a violated main. Defect B shows the blast radius: a real
god-file violation landed on main unvalidated.

**Fix approach**:

- A1 (this repo, root cause of the false verdict): add `!cancelled()` to both
  aggregate `if`s — on a cancelled run the aggregates SKIP, so every required
  context reports *no verdict* and the SM re-dispatches (the sm-kicker already
  re-arms on `workflow_run: CI completed` — any conclusion — and on non-main
  pushes). Genuine failures still arm the aggregate and still park.
- A2 (factory-side, NOT changeable from this repo): the park-clearing rule
  must accept the SM's own silent-update push (or any newer head regardless of
  author). Named here and in the PR body for the factory owner; repo-side
  tests pin the trigger surface (kicker push + workflow_run arms) this
  depends on.
- B (this repo): base state already has settings.dart back at 280/2800
  (verified: `wc -l` = 280, loc gate `[PASS] loc: 488 files within 488
  limits`). Add a repo-suite regression belt (`test/`) asserting every
  non-generated flutter_app `.dart` ≤ 2800 lines — it runs in CI `test-core`
  (no path gate) and would have failed the #2438 PR with the 2801-line file.

**Previous attempt**: none — first development leg on gh-2462.

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, model-switch-reg, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, usage-fold, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, fa-aot-build, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-portability, installer-verify, install-pin-gate, flutter-app-exzone, flutter-app-goldens, flutter-app-lock-smoke, office-addin-suite, extension-size-gate]
    if: always() && !cancelled() && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    # gh-2462: !cancelled() — a CANCELLED ci.yml run is a NON-VERDICT, never
    # a failure verdict. With plain always() the aggregate ran against legs
    # concluded `cancelled`, its fail() classified them as blockers and the
    # required check concluded FAILURE off the cancellation (run 46050811851,
    # 2026-11-27) — SM tick 46054697279 parked #2438 validation_failed off
    # that false verdict and the silent-update push could not clear its own
    # park; the human merge of fb6543e0796e landed unvalidated (#2457). On a
    # cancelled run the aggregate now SKIPS: every required context reports
    # no verdict, the sm-kicker re-arms on the completed run and the SM
    # re-dispatches fresh ci.yml. Genuine failures still arm (the park input
    # is a REAL failure only) — pinned by
    # test/ci_2462_canceled_run_no_park_guard_test.dart.
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # #1368: the publish job consumes dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict
====

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    # gh-2462: !cancelled() — same non-verdict rule as the quality-gate
    # aggregate: on a cancelled run this gate must SKIP, not run its
    # `Fail the gate` step against a cancelled binaries-pr and conclude
    # the required context FAILURE off the cancellation (the false
    # validation_failed park class, #2457). Genuine failures still arm.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # gh-1199: the boundary is now enforced at the gate's integration shard
    # SELECTION too (shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm, asserted by
    # test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart) and by
    # scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py — a live-looking integration file
    # without this tag fails the static gate. See docs/live-llm-testing.md.
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
26:#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx
33:#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
38:#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap,
  local cov_flags=""
  if stage_selected coverage; then
    cov_flags="--coverage=coverage"
    rm -rf coverage
  fi
  echo "🧪 Running dart test${cov_flags:+ with --coverage} (excluding integration tests)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $cov_flags --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  # Issue #2227: the trio rides NO quarantine filter (gh-1033: the CLI
  # coverage ratchet needs these hits pre-merge), so the #2331 loopback-ws
  # load-drop family reaches this leg unhealed — a dropped loader ws reds
  # the gate on an arbitrary victim file while every test that ran was
  # green. Same one-shot wrapper as the sharded legs: a dropped file
  # reruns ONCE (the rerun inherits --coverage=coverage — healed hits land
  # in the same coverage/ dir format_coverage merges); real failures carry
  # no ws-drop signature and stay loud. Keep the target list in sync with
  # ci.yml (test-core shard 0).
  mkdir -p build/test-results
  bash scripts/load_drop_retry.sh \
    "build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \
    "build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.retry.json" \
    -- \
    dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    $cov_flags \
    --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/cli-trio-lcov.json" \

# gh-2462 — PR description

### Root Cause

A cancelled ci.yml run delivered a FAILURE verdict to the SM: both required-check
aggregates armed on `if: always()` without a cancellation guard, ran against legs
concluded `cancelled`, and their `fail()` classified the cancellation as a
blocker — cancelled (a non-verdict) was sold to the SM as `validation_failed`.
SM tick 46054697279 parked #2438 (run 46050811851 was cancelled at 18:37Z), the
same tick's silent-update push (`2a8eb3c9`) could not clear its own park, and the
human squash-merge `fb6543e0796e` landed a tree no successful dispatch ever
validated (#2457 — the guard was right). That unvalidated tree also carried
`settings.dart` at 2801 > 2800 lines — the only gate for that ceiling
(app-crap-gate's `gates.loc`) never ran, because it sat behind the cancelled
dispatch and no repo-side belt existed for flutter_app files
(`ci_fast_gate.sh` scopes loc/crap to lib/bin core paths only).

### Previous Attempt

None — first development leg on gh-2462.

### Fix

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `!cancelled()` added to both aggregate `if`s
  (`quality-gate`, `binaries-smoke-gate`): a cancelled run now leaves every
  required context verdict-less, so the SM sees "no verdict → re-dispatch"
  (the sm-kicker already re-arms on `workflow_run: CI completed` — any
  conclusion — and on non-main pushes). Genuine failures still arm and still
  park; the skipped-security dodge and the healthy latch are unchanged.
- `test/ci_2462_canceled_run_no_park_guard_test.dart` — the repo-side SM
  decision table, EVALUATED (not grepped): cancelled run ⇒ neither aggregate
  arms (no park); genuine leg failure ⇒ aggregate arms (park works); healthy
  run ⇒ arms (latch); kicker re-arm surface pinned (`workflow_run: [CI]
  completed` + `push: branches-ignore: [main]`).
- `test/ci_2462_app_loc_ceiling_guard_test.dart` — repo-side loc-ceiling belt
  over `flutter_app` (scope/exclude/`max_lines` read from
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`); runs in CI `test-core` which has NO path
  gate, so it executes on every ci.yml dispatch — a 2801-line app file now
  fails the PR even when the validation dispatch is cancelled. The checker is
  proven against the incident shape (2801 ⇒ violation, 2800 ⇒ legal).

### Test Coverage

- `test/ci_2462_canceled_run_no_park_guard_test.dart` — RED first (both
  cancellation traps reproduced against the old `if`s), then GREEN: 9/9.
- `test/ci_2462_app_loc_ceiling_guard_test.dart` — 4/4, including the
  at-ceiling (2800 = legal) and incident (2801 = violation) fixtures.
- Full unit suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see run log below
  (no regressions; the two aggregate `if` changes are covered by the existing
  ci_* guard fleet, all green).
- `settings.dart` on this branch: 280/2800 (limit inclusive, legal);
  `crap4dart check` on the app: `[PASS] loc: 488 files within 488 limits`.

### Notes

- Factory-side remainder (external repo `dmtools-agentic-workflows`, tracked
  `@main`, NOT changeable from this repo): the park-clearing rule still
  accepts only a HUMAN push newer than the park. The ci.yml fix removes the
  only way a *non-verdict* produced a park, but after a GENUINE failure park
  the SM's own silent-update push can still deadlock validation. Factory-sm
  should accept the SM's own silent-update push (or any newer head regardless
  of author) as park-clearing. Repo-side trigger surface for that re-arm is
  pinned here.
- Tag-arm alarm semantics preserved: `ci-red-report` still treats cancelled
  legs as RED (gh-2436) and fires off the other legs' direct conclusions; the
  degraded-runner watchdog is independent of the aggregate's conclusion.
- Closes #2457 with the landed fixes: A = ci.yml `!cancelled()` on both
  required-check aggregates + the evaluated decision-table tests; B =
  settings.dart back to 280/2800 (verified on this tree) + the repo-side
  loc-ceiling belt so the app-crap-gate class can never again land uncaught.
  The validating run on the repaired tree is the ci.yml dispatch this PR's
  merge triggers (sm-merge-guard asserts its coverage on main).

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths. A blanket "everything matches" without such coverage is not verified: mark the item `fail` and run the missing cases.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
- A cancelled ci.yml run (46050811851, 2026-11-27) delivered a FAILURE verdict: both required-check aggregates (`quality-gate`, `binaries-smoke-gate`) armed on `if: always()`, ran against legs concluded `cancelled`, and their `fail()` classified cancellation as a blocker. SM tick 46054697279 parked #2438 `validation_failed`; the same tick's silent-update push (`2a8eb3c9`) could not clear the park; human merge `fb6543e0796e` landed unvalidated (#2457) with `settings.dart` 2801 > 2800 — its only gate (app-crap-gate `gates.loc`) never ran and no repo-side belt existed (loc/crap stages scope to lib/bin only).

### Previous Attempt
- None — first development leg on gh-2462.

### Fix
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `!cancelled()` on both aggregate `if`s — cancelled run ⇒ aggregates skip ⇒ every required context reports no verdict ⇒ SM re-dispatches (kicker re-arms on `workflow_run: CI completed` — any conclusion — and non-main pushes). Genuine failures still arm and park; skipped-security dodge and healthy latch unchanged.
- `test/ci_2462_canceled_run_no_park_guard_test.dart`: the repo-side SM decision table, evaluated (RED first on the old `always()`-only `if`s).
- `test/ci_2462_app_loc_ceiling_guard_test.dart`: loc-ceiling belt over flutter_app (scope/exclude/`max_lines` from `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`), runs in CI `test-core` — no path gate — so an over-ceiling app file fails every dispatch; proven against the incident shape (2801 ⇒ violation, 2800 ⇒ legal).

### Test Coverage
- New guards 9/9 + 4/4; `settings.dart` = 280/2800 on this tree; `crap4dart check`: `[PASS] loc: 488 files within 488 limits`; ci_*/release_* guard fleet 834 green; root `dart analyze` clean; full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`) — see run note below.

### Notes
- Factory-side remainder (external `dmtools-agentic-workflows`, tracked `@main`, not changeable here): park-clearing still demands a HUMAN push — it should accept the SM's own silent-update push (or any newer head) as park-clearing; repo-side trigger surface is pinned.
- Tag-arm alarm preserved: `ci-red-report` still treats cancelled legs as RED (gh-2436).
- #2457 can be closed with these landed fixes (A + B); the validating run on the repaired tree is the ci.yml dispatch this merge triggers.

Replace the whole text each time (the newest call wins); `working_set("")` clears it. The cap is 4096 chars: a longer text is refused, not clipped — shorten it and call again.
